title: Northstar firewall state desync - postmortem + oncall runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the incident that affected the Northstar private deployment on 2026-10-14 where control-plane reachability from customer worker nodes degraded intermittently after a customer-side firewall change. Impact: some inference traffic experienced 5–30s stalls; control plane healthchecks between agents and central controlplane dropped to UNREACHABLE for ~12 minutes for a subset (~22%) of nodes. No data was lost, but customer observed degraded request tail-latency and opened a Sev1.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2026-10-14 01:03: customer applied new DNAT/port-mapping rules on their perimeter firewall (we observed traceroutes change at 01:04).
- 2026-10-14 01:06: central monitoring triggered elevated agent error rates (conntrack mismatches, TCP RST seen).
- 2026-10-14 01:08: first oncall alerted; engineers started packet captures and checked conntrack counters on affected NAT gateways.
- 2026-10-14 01:12: partial rollback suggested to customer; customer unable to rollback immediately due to change freeze policy.
- 2026-10-14 01:20: we applied temporary keepalive policy (1s UDP keepalive for controlplane-heartbeat) via agent-side config; controlplane reachability recovered for most nodes by 01:24.
- 2026-10-14 01:35: full mitigation in place: updated conntrack max entries and added conservative NAT timeout overrides on affected customer-edge boxes (coord with customer ops).
- 2026-10-14 01:45: incident declared mitigated; monitoring stable. Postmortem investigation continued.

Symptoms observed:
- controlplane heartbeats missing from ~22% of agents in a single AZ; agents reported repeated connect() followed by immediate RST from remote.
- tcpdump showed SYN/SYN-ACK sequence, but subsequent data packets dropped or replaced by RSTs from firewall.
- conntrack table on customer NAT devices showed large number of entries in TIME_WAIT/ASSURED, nearing capacity.
- no CPU/memory pressure on agents or controlplane pods.

Immediate mitigation actions (what we did during oncall):
- collection: captured 60s tcpdump on agent, NAT box, and load-balancer. Uploaded to incident folder on Confluence.
- increased agent heartbeat frequency temporarily (to 1s) to keep entries active in customer's conntrack table so NAT did not garbage collect necessary mappings.
- recommended to customer: increase conntrack max and lower TCP/UDP ephemeral timeout for NAT (we provided specific sysctl commands).
- rolled out quick instrumentation to log conntrack hit/miss counters from agent-side proxy to Sentry/Grafana for next 48h.

Root cause analysis (current hypothesis):
1) Customer firewall change introduced asymmetric pathing for agent->controlplane and controlplane->agent flows (DNAT applied in one direction only on a subset of boxes).
2) The asymmetric NAT plus relatively aggressive conntrack timeouts caused ephemeral mappings to be garbage collected between the handshake and data flows, leading the firewall to respond with RSTs or drop packets.
3) Our agents rely on long-lived TCP connections and expect stateful path symmetry; under asymmetric NAT the controlplane TCP flows became fragile under high NAT churn.
4) Conntrack table exhaustion on a few NAT devices (configured low by customer for historical reasons) magnified the issue when heartbeat intervals increased.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- tcpdump from NAT showed SYN/SYN-ACK but later packets from controlplane mapped to different ephemeral ports -> conntrack mismatch.
- conntrack counters (nf_conntrack) showed many entries with lifetime near timeout window; after we increased keepalive, entries stayed ASSURED longer and connections did not reset.
- traceroute/AS-path differences before/after change correlate to customer DNAT mapping changes.

What didn't cause it:
- not a bug in our TLS stack (handshakes completed).
- not a CPU/memory failure on controlplane (no resource spikes).
- not a load-balancer software upgrade coincidentally applied (confirmed with infra schedules).

Runbook draft - triage checklist for oncall (quick steps, keep simple):
1) Confirm symptoms: check controlplane/agent heartbeat dashboards; identify affected nodes.
2) Run tcpdump (30–60s) on agent(s) and edge NAT (if customer allows) capturing SYN,SYN-ACK,ACK and RSTs.
3) Query nf_conntrack counters on NAT gateway: total entries, entries per-namespace (if applicable), TIME_WAIT count.
4) If RSTs observed and conntrack nearing capacity: recommend increasing nf_conntrack_max to at least current_entries*2 and reduce timeout for ephemeral UDP/TCP where safe. Provide commands: 
   - sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
   - sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=432000 (tune down only if safe)
5) Enable temporary agent keepalives: set controlplane.agent.heartbeat_interval=1s (rolling restart of agent) to keep NAT mappings alive while customer applies longer-term fixes.
6) If the customer cannot change firewall immediately, enable our fallback routing policy: route controlplane traffic via alternate regional egress if available (see routing playbook id: routing-fallback-v2).
7) Escalate to customer network team and share packet captures and conntrack dumps.
8) After connectivity returns, collect post-incident captures and mark incident for postmortem.

Longer-term remediations and action items (owners and tentative deadlines):
- Add automated detection for asymmetric pathing: compare src/dst ports seen at agent and at controlplane for samples (Owner: Samir Rao, ETA: 2026-10-30).
- Default keepalive policy: implement adaptive keepalives that step up when conntrack churn detected (Owner: Ethan Park, ETA: 2026-11-07).
- Doc: best-practice checklist for customer NAT/firewall settings when onboarding private deployments; include recommended conntrack_max ranges by expected QPS (Owner: Mariana Ortiz, ETA: 2026-10-22).
- Improve observability: ship conntrack-level metrics from our on-prem sidecar where customer allows (Owner: Alex Chen, ETA: 2026-11-14).
- Upgrade onboarding question checklist: require customers to disclose DNAT/load-balancer patterns and default ephemeral port ranges (Owner: Solutions Eng, ETA: 2026-10-21).

Metrics and impact:
- Affected nodes: 22% of agents (subset in customer AZ-3).
- Peak dropped heartbeats: 1,120 over 12 minutes.
- Customer-reported increased 95th/99th token latency during window: +27% / +62%.

Notes to self / informal observations (raw):
- Customer had a silent change freeze but allowed emergency tweaks after we showed packet dumps.
- The NAT boxes were appliance-based with firmware that hides some conntrack internals; used heuristics to map entries. This slowed pairing evidence collection.
- Keepalive trick felt hacky but bought us breathing room; need to ensure it doesn't produce higher load for low-resource devices.

Open questions (for the next investigation session):
- Could our agent be modified to detect and automatically fall back when it detects asymmetric NAT? (fast path vs keepalive policy)
- Are there any negative side-effects observed from short keepalives on customer billing (bandwidth/cost) or appliance CPU? We must track after rollout.
- Is there a way to pre-scan customer-perimeter NAT configuration during onboarding to identify risky setups?

Appendix - useful snippets (pulled from captures):
- tcpdump excerpt (agent side):
  01:06:11.123456 IP agent-node.43210 > controlplane.lb.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
  01:06:11.123789 IP controlplane.lb.443 > agent-node.43210: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 65160, length 0
  01:06:11.124100 IP agent-node.43210 > controlplane.lb.443: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0   <-- unexpected R after SYN-ACK

- conntrack dump (customer NAT device):
  tcp 6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.1.7.12 dst=54.210.33.8 sport=43210 dport=443 src2=54.210.33.8 dst2=203.0.113.5 sport2=443 dport2=43210 [ASSURED] mark=0
  tcp 6 29 TIME_WAIT src=10.1.7.15 dst=54.210.33.8 sport=49877 dport=443 ...

- quick grep from agent logs:
  2026-10-14T01:06:11Z ERROR agent connectivity: remote reset after handshake for peer=controlplane.lb:443 conn_id=7a9b

Post-incident communication plan:
- Send initial postmortem to customer ops with timeline and recommended config changes by 2026-10-16.
- Internal postmortem draft to ENG and SRE channels; schedule 30m retro on 2026-10-20.
- Track action item progress in NORTH-1234 and link to this doc.

Status / next steps:
- Mitigation complete and monitored for 72h window; no recurrence so far.
- Owners assigned for follow-ups above.
- Next deep-dive scheduled with customer network team on 2026-10-19 to audit NAT/firewall appliance firmware and config.

If you were oncall and want a 1-page cheat sheet:
- Check heartbeats -> tcpdump -> conntrack counters -> enable keepalive -> ask customer to bump conntrack_max OR rollback DNAT change.

-- Priya (notes, draft)
